desc: **Task 1 (theory verification):** Confirmed every non-isolated vertex is adjacent to A=argmin R or B=argmax L, all non-isolated vertices form a single component (so −1 ⟺ s or t isolated), and that optimal paths need at most 4 vertices with exactly the enumerated candidate forms (domination proof re-verified for the "both intermediates on the same side" case via the contradiction L_t ≤ R_a < L_s ≤ R_b < L_t).

**Task 2 (implementation):** Full O(N+Q) program written — prefix-min `prefR`, suffix-min `sufL` with INF sentinels and correct off-by-one indexing (`pR[L-1]`, `sL[R+1]`, arrays sized 2N+2), isolation test, three candidate families with INF guards, fast bulk I/O.

**Task 3 (validation):** Verified candidate-uniqueness/validity arguments (intermediates provably distinct from s, t and from each other whenever the candidate is not dominated by the base case) and hand-traced both samples: sample 1 → 11 / 6 / −1; sample 2 → 157 (direct edge) / 124 (direct edge) / −1 (vertex 7 isolated) / 114 / 114 (3-vertex candidate with minLeft(6)=32).

**Task 4 (performance check):** Query loop uses local aliases (`pR`, `sL`, `Lloc`, `Rloc`, `Wloc`), no per-query function calls, single `sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()` parse and one joined write — comfortably handles N,Q = 2×10⁵.
